Jorre: Flemish short form of Joris or Jordaan, forms of George (Greek 'farmer') or Jordan (Hebrew 'to flow down').
Maite: Spanish and Basque, meaning 'beloved'. Also a Spanish form of Maria Teresa.
Oumaima: Arabic Umayma, a diminutive of umm 'mother', meaning 'little mother'. Moroccan spelling.
Jorn: Scandinavian and Dutch variant of Jörn, a Low German form of Jørgen (George), from Greek 'farmer'.
Remco: Dutch and Frisian short form of Remmert or Reinout, from Germanic 'counsel' and 'power'.
Ewout: Dutch, from Germanic 'ever' or 'law' and 'rule'; a form of Evert/Ewald. Uncertain.
Déborah: French form of Deborah, from Hebrew 'bee'. The biblical judge.
Rube: Short form of Reuben, from Hebrew 'behold, a son'. Also a rural nickname in English.
Gil: Hebrew 'joy', or a short form of Gilbert or Egidius (Greek 'young goat'). Also Portuguese form of Giles.
Yentl: Yiddish, from the Italian Yentl, perhaps meaning 'gentle' (Old French gentil). Known from Isaac Bashevis Singer.
Timon: Greek, from timao 'to honour, value'. Known from Shakespeare's Timon of Athens.
Shanna: Probably a variant of Shannon or Shana, Irish 'old' or Hebrew 'beautiful'. Uncertain.
Yarno: Probably a Dutch or Frisian coinage, perhaps linked to Jaro or Arno ('eagle'). Origin uncertain.
Joni: Short form of Joan or Jonathan; also a Finnish form of John, from Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Lieselotte: Dutch and German compound of Liese and Lotte, from Elisabeth and Charlotte.
Cara: Italian and Latin for 'dear', or Irish 'friend'.
Coraline: Modern English elaboration of Cora, from Greek kore 'maiden'. Popularised by Neil Gaiman's novel.
Savannah: English, from the Spanish word sabana 'treeless plain'. Used as a modern American name.
Liesl: Austrian and German diminutive of Elisabeth, from Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Lisse: Dutch short form of Elisabeth or Liselotte; also a Dutch place name. From Hebrew 'my God is an oath'.
Matthijs: Dutch form of Matthew, from Hebrew 'gift of God'.
Yoni: Hebrew diminutive of Jonathan, 'God has given'. Also Sanskrit for 'source'.
Davy: English and Dutch diminutive of David, from Hebrew 'beloved'.
Jasmien: Dutch form of Jasmine, from Persian yasmin, the flower.
Jitske: Frisian diminutive of Jitte or Jette, ultimately from Germanic names like Judith (Hebrew 'praised'). Uncertain.
Mickaël: French form of Michael, from Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Annelien: Dutch compound of Anne and Lien, from Hebrew Hannah 'grace' and short form of Caroline or Helena.
Loubna: Arabic Lubna, a type of tree resin (storax) and also 'milky'. Moroccan spelling.
Axana: Probably a variant of Roxana, from Persian 'bright, dawn'. Origin uncertain.
Ayse: Turkish form of Aisha, Arabic 'alive, living'. Name of the Prophet's wife.
Cassandre: French form of Cassandra, from Greek Kassandra, the prophetess of Troy.
Nikki: English short form of Nicole or Nicola, from Greek 'victory of the people'.
Soukaina: Arabic Sukayna, a diminutive of sakina 'tranquility, peace'.
Bérénice: French form of Berenice, from Macedonian Greek 'bringer of victory'.
Yenthe: Flemish modern name, probably from Jente or Yentl. Origin uncertain.
Redouane: French spelling of Arabic Ridwan, meaning 'good pleasure, approval' and the guardian of Paradise.
Stéphane: French form of Stephen, from Greek stephanos 'crown, garland'.
Enrique: Spanish form of Henry, from Germanic 'home ruler'.
Nolhan: Breton and French variant of Nolan or Noël. Probably 'champion'. Origin uncertain.
Arjen: Dutch and Frisian form of Adrian or Arie, from Latin 'from Hadria' or Hebrew 'lion'. Uncertain.
Kadir: Turkish and Arabic Qadir, meaning 'powerful, capable', an attribute of God.
Thibe: Flemish short form of Thibaut or Theobald, Germanic 'people' and 'bold'.
Maéva: Breton or Tahitian, from Tahitian maeva 'welcome'. Also a French blend of Marie and Eva.
Jérémie: French form of Jeremiah, from Hebrew 'God will exalt'.
Geike: Frisian and Dutch diminutive of Gea or Geertje, Germanic 'spear'. Origin uncertain.
Brahim: Arabic, a Maghrebi form of Ibrahim (Abraham), meaning 'father of many'.
Auke: Frisian, a short form of Aucke, from Germanic 'rich, prosperous'. Here a girls' name.
Morgan: Welsh, probably 'sea-born' or 'sea circle'. Used for both sexes.
Neal: English and Irish form of Niall, possibly 'cloud', 'champion' or 'passionate'.
Kathleen: Anglicised Irish Caitlín, form of Catherine, from Greek 'pure'.
Lalie: French short form of Eulalie, from Greek 'well-spoken'.
Jodie: English diminutive of Judith, from Hebrew 'praised', or of Joseph.
Ignace: French and Dutch form of Ignatius, from Latin Ignatius, linked to ignis 'fire'.
Kayleigh: Modern English, probably from Kay with Irish Caoilfhionn or place-name -leigh. Meaning uncertain.
Sebastien: French form of Sebastian, from Greek 'from Sebaste', meaning 'venerable'.
Lissa: Short form of Melissa or Elisabeth; Greek 'honey bee'. Also Greek 'rage'.
Annelore: German compound of Anne and Lore (Eleonora), from Hebrew 'grace' and uncertain.
Batuhan: Turkish, from bat 'west' and han 'ruler': 'ruler of the west'.
Jelena: Slavic form of Helen, from Greek 'torch' or 'bright'.
Sinem: Turkish, probably 'my bosom, breast', also a Turkish poetic word. Used as a girls' name.
Kiano: Probably a modern coinage, perhaps from Kian or Keanu. Origin uncertain.
Xena: Modern name from the TV series, based on Greek xenos 'stranger, guest'.
Wietse: Frisian, a short form of Wiebe or Wiet, from Germanic 'war'. Origin uncertain.
Ymke: Frisian and Dutch diminutive of Ymke, from Germanic 'whole, universal' (Imke, Emma). Uncertain.
Shane: Anglicised Irish Seán, a form of John, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Shawn: Anglicised Irish Seán, a form of John, Hebrew 'God is gracious'.
Oriane: French, from Latin oriens 'rising' or aurum 'gold'; possibly from the medieval romance Amadis de Gaula.
Alessandra: Italian feminine of Alexander, from Greek 'defender of men'.
Lydie: French form of Lydia, from Greek 'woman from Lydia', a region in Asia Minor.
Cyprien: French form of Cyprian, from Latin Cyprianus, 'from Cyprus'.
Gino: Italian short form of names ending in -gino, such as Luigi or Giorgino.
Yasemin: Turkish form of jasmine, from Persian yasmin.
Elyse: Variant of Elise or Elysia, from Elisabeth (Hebrew 'my God is an oath') or from Elysium.
Wiebe: Frisian and Dutch, a short form of Wigbold or Wibe, from Germanic 'war'.
Marissa: Latin and Spanish, from 'of the sea' (maris); a form of Maris.
Ronan: Irish and Breton, from Rónán, diminutive of rón 'seal'.
Soukaïna: Arabic Sukayna, a diminutive of sakina 'tranquility, peace'.
Alexi: Finnish and Greek diminutive of Alexis or Alexander, 'defender'.
Emine: Turkish form of Amina, Arabic 'faithful, trustworthy'.
Karsten: North German and Danish variant of Carsten, a form of Christian, Latin 'follower of Christ'.
Kassandra: Greek, from Kassandra, the Trojan prophetess; meaning uncertain.
Luc: French form of Luke, from Greek Loukas, 'man from Lucania'.
Gladys: Welsh, from Gwladus, probably 'ruler' or 'princess'. Possibly a form of Claudia.
Nihad: Arabic, meaning 'chest' or 'bosom'. Used for both sexes, in the Balkans for boys.
Tracy: English, from a Norman surname meaning 'from Tracy', a place in Normandy, and used as a first name.
Tiemen: Frisian and Dutch form of Tiemen, from Germanic 'people'. Related to Timon or Thieme. Uncertain.
Erine: Probably a variant of Irene, Greek 'peace', or a modern Dutch coinage. Uncertain.
Nicky: English diminutive of Nicholas or Nicola, from Greek 'victory of the people'.
Sandrine: French diminutive of Alexandrine, from Greek 'defender'.
Othmane: Maghrebi spelling of Uthman, Arabic 'young bustard'. Borne by the third caliph.
Jarod: English variant of Jared, from Hebrew 'descent' or 'rose'.
Alissia: Elaboration of Alicia or Alissa, from Germanic 'noble kind'.
Hatim: Arabic, meaning 'judge' or 'decisive'. Known from the generous poet Hatim al-Tai.
Lennart: Scandinavian and Dutch form of Leonard, from Germanic 'brave lion'.
Natasha: Russian diminutive of Natalya, from Latin natalis 'birthday', i.e. Christmas.
Toby: English form of Tobias, from Hebrew Tovyah, 'God is good'.
Nesrine: Arabic, from nisrin 'wild rose' or 'dog rose'.
Zia: Arabic 'light, radiance'; also Italian 'aunt' and Zia a short form in some cultures.
Randy: English diminutive of Randall or Randolph, from Germanic 'shield' and 'wolf'.
Adnane: Arabic Adnan, the ancestor of the northern Arabs; meaning 'settler' or 'resident'.
Fiebe: Frisian, a form of Febe, from Phoebe, Greek 'bright'. Also Frisian male Fiebe.
Dany: Short form of Daniel, from Hebrew 'God is my judge'.
Jaron: Hebrew, 'to sing, to shout', or a form of Jason or Jared. Uncertain.
Betül: Turkish, from Arabic batul, meaning 'virgin' or 'devoted'. Epithet of Fatima.
Chanel: French, from the surname Chanel, 'canal' or 'channel pipe'. Popularised by the fashion house.
Ewoud: Dutch, from Germanic 'ever' or 'law' and 'rule'; a form of Ewout or Eward. Uncertain.
Liselotte: German compound of Liese and Lotte, from Elisabeth and Charlotte.
Nolwenn: Breton, from nol 'Christmas' and gwenn 'white, blessed', or 'holy'. Also Nolwenn Leroy.
Chiel: Dutch short form of Michiel, from Hebrew 'who is like God?'.
Cyrielle: French feminine of Cyril, from Greek kyrios 'lord'.
Catho: Short form of Catherine or Catholique, from Greek 'pure'. Used informally in Belgium.
Stephen: English form of Greek Stephanos, 'crown, garland'.
Jara: Czech, Slovak and Slavic short form of Jaroslava, 'fierce glory'. Also Spanish 'rockrose'.
Jitte: Frisian, a form of Jette or Judith, 'praised'. Uncertain.
Ilano: Probably a modern coinage, perhaps from Italian and Hebrew ilan 'tree'. Origin uncertain.
Kübra: Turkish, from Arabic kubra, meaning 'greatest, the greater'.
Théophile: French, from Greek theophilos, 'loved by God' or 'friend of God'.
Mirco: Italian short form of Domenico or Americo, from Latin 'of the Lord'. Uncertain.
Cyrille: French form of Cyril, from Greek kyrios 'lord'.
Morena: Spanish and Italian, meaning 'dark-haired, brunette'. Also Slavic Morana.
Delano: English and French, from a surname meaning 'of the night', or 'from the nut tree'. Uncertain.
Jelte: Frisian, a form of Jelle, from Germanic 'to pay, tribute'. Possibly 'valued'.
Debora: Italian, Spanish and Dutch form of Deborah, Hebrew 'bee'.
Maïly: Modern French coinage, probably from Maïlys or Maelys. Origin uncertain.
Calogero: Sicilian, from Greek kalogeros, 'good elder', also 'monk'. Named after a Sicilian saint.
Siska: Dutch and Czech short form of Francisca, from Latin 'Frenchwoman'.
Titouan: Breton and French diminutive of Titus or Tite, from Latin Titus, uncertain meaning.
Gary: English, from a surname from Old English 'spear', and a short form of Gareth or Gerald.
Ilena: Variant of Ilona or Elena, Hungarian and Slavic forms of Helen, Greek 'torch'.
Marnix: Dutch and Flemish, a variant of Marinus or Marnix, Latin 'of the sea'. Famous for Marnix van Sint-Aldegonde.
Alain: French and Breton, from Alan, probably meaning 'little rock' or 'harmony'. Origin uncertain.
Bouchra: Arabic Bushra, meaning 'good news, glad tidings'. Moroccan spelling.
Nawfal: Arabic, meaning 'generous giver, ocean' or 'one who gives freely'.
Maylis: Gascon and Basque form of Mary Lise, from Mary and Elizabeth, or Maï. Uncertain.
Nieke: Dutch and Frisian diminutive of Nicolaas or Veronica; possibly from Greek 'victory'.
Victorine: French feminine diminutive of Victor, from Latin victor 'conqueror'.
Clélia: French form of Clelia, from a Roman family name; possibly 'glory' (Greek kleos).
Kitana: Modern name popularised by the Mortal Kombat game; probably from Japanese katana 'sword'. Origin uncertain.
Ameline: French, a form of Amalia or Emeline, from Germanic amal 'work'.
Naomy: Variant of Naomi, from Hebrew na'omi 'my pleasantness'.
Tyron: Variant of Tyrone, Irish 'land of Eoghan'. Also known from actor Tyrone Power.
Batiste: French form of Baptiste, from Greek baptistes 'baptizer'.
Aagje: Dutch and Frisian diminutive of Agatha or Agnes, from Greek 'good' or 'pure'.
Wassila: Arabic Wasila, meaning 'means of approach, link'. Maghrebi spelling.
Anouchka: Russian diminutive of Anna, from Hebrew 'grace', popular in French-speaking countries.
Indy: English short form of Indiana or Indigo; known from Indiana Jones. Used as a modern name.
Lovely: English word, meaning 'beautiful'. A modern given name; also used in Filipino and Indian communities.
Okan: Turkish, from oka, 'to be like a god'. Origin uncertain.
Armelle: Breton, from Gwenn Armel; Armel from Celtic arth 'bear' and mael 'prince'.
Hippolyte: French form of Hippolytus, from Greek 'horse' and 'to loosen'. A figure in Greek myth.
Medine: Turkish and Arabic form of Madina, meaning 'city', after the holy city.
Stiene: Dutch diminutive of Christiena or Stientje, from Christina, Greek 'follower of Christ'.
Andries: Dutch form of Andrew, from Greek andreios 'manly, brave'.
Asli: Turkish Aslı, meaning 'genuine' or 'original'. Also the heroine of the legend Kerem and Aslı.
Matiz: Probably a Spanish word matiz 'shade, nuance', or a variant of Mathis. Origin uncertain.
Kristina: Form of Christina, from Latin christianus 'follower of Christ'.
Rick: English and Dutch short form of Richard, from Germanic 'brave ruler'.
Ylan: Variant of Ilan, Hebrew for 'tree'. Also Turkish 'snake'.
Orlane: French modern name, possibly from Orlando or Roland, Germanic 'fame of the land'. Uncertain.
Anse: Flemish short form of Anna or Anselm; Germanic 'god-protection' for Anselm. Uncertain.
Jenthe: Flemish modern name, probably from Jente or Jan 'God is gracious'. Here a girls' name; origin uncertain.
Torben: Danish and North German, from Old Norse Thorbjorn, 'Thor's bear'.
Cristina: Italian, Spanish and Romanian form of Christina, Latin 'follower of Christ'.
Loane: French modern name, probably from Loïc or Joan. Origin uncertain.
Maëline: French modern name, probably a blend of Maëlle and Line, or from Mathilde. Origin uncertain.
Amory: English, from Amaury, Germanic 'work' and 'rule'. Also a French place name.
Bastiaan: Dutch form of Sebastian, from Greek 'from Sebaste', 'venerable'.
Dilan: Kurdish and Turkish, meaning 'heart' or 'loving'; also a variant of Dylan.
Karlijn: Dutch form of Caroline, from Charles, Germanic 'free man'.
Chayma: Arabic Shaymaa, 'beauty mark' or 'having a beauty spot'. Tunisian spelling.
Marijn: Dutch, from Latin marinus, 'of the sea'. Used for both sexes.
Reinout: Dutch form of Reynold, from Germanic 'counsel' and 'rule'.
Chadi: Arabic Shadi, meaning 'singer' or 'one who sings'. French spelling.
Elanur: Turkish, from ela 'hazel' and nur 'light'; meaning 'hazel light'.
Haley: English, from a surname meaning 'hay clearing' or 'ingenious' in Irish. Used as a modern girls' name.
Mies: Dutch diminutive of Maria. From Hebrew Miriam.
Noha: Arabic, meaning 'intellect, reason, wisdom'. Used for girls and boys.
Diogo: Portuguese form of Diego, probably from Greek 'doubly born', or from Spanish Santiago. Uncertain.
Salaheddine: Arabic Salah ad-Din, 'righteousness of the faith'. The medieval sultan Saladin.
